explanations: Buckets range 0 to 99, but the comparison is `bucket <= rolloutPercent`. At rolloutPercent 0, every user in bucket 0 (about 1%) still gets the flag, so an enabled flag set to 0% is not actually off; at 10% roughly 11% of users are in. For `require-mfa-enrollment` this means a 'dark' rollout still locks out about 1% of users without MFA. The comparison should be `bucket < rolloutPercent`.
isEnabled returns false on the deny check before it ever looks at allowTenants. Buckets are only consulted after both lists, and load() validates only rolloutPercent.

Including the flag key decorrelates rollouts: a user in the first 5% of one flag is not automatically in the first 5% of every other flag. The bucket is still stable per user and flag, cost is unchanged, and tenantId is not hashed.

The passkey branch requires hasWebAuthn, so it is skipped; hasTotp is true, so decide returns the TOTP challenge before the enrollment flag is evaluated. Denial applies only to users with no second factor.
